target.title: fix(config): render validation array indices with brackets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config validation diagnostics currently render numeric Zod path segments with dot notation in terminal output, so array indexes look like object properties. For example, an invalid value under an agent list can surface to a human reader as `agents.list.3.tools.profile`, which is harder to read than `agents.list[3].tools.profile`.

This is a narrow, partial improvement related to #104854. It only addresses human-facing array-index path formatting for config validation diagnostics; it does not add line numbers or offending-value (`got`) rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ConfigValidationIssue.path` is a documented machine-readable dot path and is serialized through `openclaw config validate --json`. The reviewer correctly pointed out that changing that shared field to bracket notation would be a compatibility break for scripts and sibling consumers.

This revision keeps the shared validation path contract unchanged and moves bracket notation to the terminal issue-formatting boundary only. JSON output and normalized/shared validation issues continue to use dot paths such as `agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting`.

The display formatter is root-aware: it uses the parsed config tree to bracket numeric path segments only when the parent value is actually an array. Numeric object keys from record-like config surfaces, such as `diagnostics.otel.headers.0`, stay dotted.

## User Impact

Users reading non-JSON config validation errors can now distinguish arrays from object properties:

```text
Before: agents.list.3.tools.profile: Invalid input
After:  agents.list[3].tools.profile: Invalid input
```

Machine-readable consumers keep the existing representation:

```json
{
  "path": "agents.list.3.tools.profile",
  "message": "Invalid input"
}
```

Numeric record keys are intentionally not rewritten as arrays:

```text
diagnostics.otel.headers.0: Invalid input
```

## Evidence

Focused regression coverage now asserts both display and contract behavior:

```ts
formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
  {
    pathStyle: "display",
    pathRoot: { agents: { list: [{ tools: { exec: { commandHighlighting: "bad" } } }] } },
  },
) -> "- agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"

formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "diagnostics.otel.headers.0", message: "Expected string" },
  "-",
  {
    pathStyle: "display",
    pathRoot: { diagnostics: { otel: { headers: { "0": false } } } },
  },
) -> "- diagnostics.otel.headers.0: Expected string"

formatConfigIssueLine(
  { path: "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting", message: "Expected boolean" },
  "-",
) -> "- agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Expected boolean"
```

Direct CLI proof on the repaired head (`df57b0fc55`) used a real config file with both an invalid array item and an invalid numeric record key:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "list": [
      {
        "id": "proof-agent",
        "name": "Proof Agent",
        "tools": { "exec": { "commandHighlighting": "bad" } }
      }
    ]
  },
  "diagnostics": { "otel": { "headers": { "0": false } } }
}
```

Terminal validation output now brackets only the array segment and preserves the numeric record key:

```text
openclaw config validate
OpenClaw config is invalid: <repo>/.artifacts/pr104935-proof/openclaw-invalid-config.json
  diagnostics.otel.headers.0: Invalid input: expected string, received boolean
  agents.list[0].tools.exec.commandHighlighting: Invalid input: expected boolean, received string (allowed: true, false)
terminal_exit=1
```

JSON validation output keeps both paths dotted:

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "issues": [
    {
      "path": "diagnostics.otel.headers.0",
      "message": "Invalid input: expected string, received boolean"
    },
    {
      "path": "agents.list.0.tools.exec.commandHighlighting",
      "message": "Invalid input: expected boolean, received string (allowed: true, false)",
      "allowedValues": ["true", "false"]
    }
  ]
}
```

The proof assertions from the same run were:

```json
{
  "terminal_has_array_bracket": true,
  "terminal_has_numeric_record_dot": true,
  "terminal_has_wrong_numeric_record_bracket": false,
  "json_has_array_dot": true,
  "json_has_numeric_record_dot": true,
  "json_has_array_bracket": false,
  "terminal_exit": 1,
  "json_exit": 1
}
```

Validation run locally on the review-fix revision:

```powershell
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --reporter verbose
corepack pnpm@11.2.2 -C D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw-pr104935-reviewfix-worktree exec vitest run src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.cli.config.ts --no-file-parallelism --pool threads --testNamePattern "path|config validate|numeric path|JSON|numeric string" --reporter verbose
git diff --check -- src/cli/config-cli.test.ts src/cli/config-cli.ts src/config/issue-format.test.ts src/config/issue-format.ts src/config/validation.test.ts src/config/validation.ts
```

Results:

- formatter + validation focused run: `2 passed`, `44 tests passed`
- CLI focused run covering `config validate`, `--json`, and numeric path cases: `1 passed`, `49 tests passed`, `81 skipped`
- `git diff --check`: passed

A previously attempted focused `config-misc` single-test run timed out inside the existing async snapshot test body after 120s. The touched assertion in that file is only the expected path string (`agents.list[0].sandbox` -> `agents.list.0.sandbox`), and the narrower validation/CLI tests above cover the requested contract directly.

## Possible call chain / impact

```text
config validation failure
  -> Zod issue path array
  -> mapZodIssueToConfigIssue()
  -> ConfigValidationIssue.path remains dot-path
  -> config validate --json serializes the dot-path issue unchanged
  -> non-JSON config validate output calls formatConfigIssueLines(..., { pathStyle: "display", pathRoot: snapshot.parsed })
  -> terminal diagnostics bracket numeric segments only when the parsed parent value is an array
```

Affected surface is limited to human-facing `config validate` issue rendering for numeric array-index path segments. This PR intentionally leaves shared validation issue objects, JSON output, numeric record keys, config parsing, config get/set path syntax, plugin schema diagnostics, source line-number lookup, and bad-value rendering unchanged.

Related: #104854
